# Fundamental Group of $S_{g,m}$

**Answer-leak check:** The problem statement contains only the question, no solutions, sketches, or answer values. Proceeding.

---

## Setup and Notation

Let $S_{g,m}$ denote the **orientable** surface of genus $g$ with $m$ punctures (i.e., $m$ points removed from the closed surface $S_{g,0}$). We determine $\pi_1(S_{g,m})$ for all $g \geq 0$, $m \geq 0$.

---

## Step 1. A Cell Decomposition of $S_{g,m}$

Start from the standard CW-structure on the closed surface $S_{g,0}$:

- One $0$-cell $v$,
- $2g$ open $1$-cells $a_1, b_1, \dots, a_g, b_g$,
- One open $2$-cell $e^2$, attached along the loop
$$\omega = [a_1, b_1]\,[a_2, b_2]\cdots[a_g, b_g], \qquad [a,b] = aba^{-1}b^{-1}.$$

Now form $S_{g,m}$ by removing $m$ points $p_1, \dots, p_m$ from the **interior** of $e^2$. Around each $p_i$ choose a small embedded loop $c_i$ (based at a point on $\partial e^2$ via a thin corridor). The punctured $2$-cell $e^2 \setminus \{p_1,\dots,p_m\}$ deformation-retracts onto the graph
$$\Gamma = \partial e^2 \;\cup\; \bigcup_{i=1}^{m} \bigl(\text{corridor to } c_i \cup c_i\bigr),$$
i.e., the boundary circle together with $m$ loops tethered to it. Thus $S_{g,m}$ is homotopy equivalent to the quotient space obtained from $\Gamma$ by identifying $\partial e^2$ according to $\omega$.

---

## Step 2. Applying van Kampen — the Presentation

The $1$-skeleton of $S_{g,m}$ (after the retraction) carries generators
$$a_1, b_1, \dots, a_g, b_g,\; c_1, \dots, c_m,$$
where the $c_i$ are loops around the punctures. Reading off the attaching map of the (punctured) $2$-cell gives the single relation
$$[a_1,b_1]\,[a_2,b_2]\cdots[a_g,b_g]\;c_1\,c_2\cdots c_m = 1.$$

Hence, by the Seifert–van Kampen theorem:

$$\boxed{\pi_1(S_{g,m}) \;=\; \bigl\langle a_1,b_1,\dots,a_g,b_g,\,c_1,\dots,c_m \;\big|\; [a_1,b_1]\cdots[a_g,b_g]\,c_1\cdots c_m = 1 \bigr\rangle.}$$

This is the **standard presentation** valid for all $g \geq 0$, $m \geq 0$.

---

## Step 3. Closed Case ($m = 0$): the Surface Group

When $m=0$ there are no $c_i$ generators, and the presentation becomes

$$\pi_1(S_{g,0}) = \bigl\langle a_1,b_1,\dots,a_g,b_g \;\big|\; [a_1,b_1]\cdots[a_g,b_g] = 1 \bigr\rangle.$$

This is the **orientable surface group** of genus $g$. It is a one-relator group on $2g$ generators; for $g \geq 1$ it is **not free** (its abelianization is $\mathbb{Z}^{2g}$, but the group is non-abelian and has cohomological dimension $2$). For $g = 0$ the presentation has no generators and the trivial relation, giving $\pi_1(S^2) = \{1\}$, as expected.

---

## Step 4. Punctured Case ($m \geq 1$): a Free Group

When $m \geq 1$, the single relation
$$c_m = \bigl(c_1 \cdots c_{m-1}\bigr)^{-1}\,[a_g,b_g]^{-1}\cdots[a_1,b_1]^{-1}$$
expresses $c_m$ as a word in the remaining $2g + m - 1$ generators. Eliminating $c_m$ via Tietze transformation yields a **free** presentation:

$$\pi_1(S_{g,m}) \;\cong\; F_{2g + m - 1}, \qquad m \geq 1,$$

the free group of rank $2g + m - 1$.

### Verification via Euler characteristic

$S_{g,m}$ has $\chi(S_{g,m}) = 2 - 2g - m$. For $m \geq 1$ the surface is non-compact and deformation-retracts onto a connected graph $\Gamma$ with $\chi(\Gamma) = 2 - 2g - m$. A connected graph with $\chi = 1 - r$ has $\pi_1 \cong F_r$, so
$$r = 1 - (2 - 2g - m) = 2g + m - 1. \qquad \checkmark$$

### Consistency checks

| $(g,m)$ | Surface | Predicted $\pi_1$ | Known value |
|---|---|---|---|
| $(0,0)$ | $S^2$ | trivial (closed, $g=0$) | $\{1\}$ ✓ |
| $(0,1)$ | $S^2\setminus\{\text{pt}\} \cong \mathbb{R}^2$ | $F_{0} = \{1\}$ | $\{1\}$ ✓ |
| $(0,2)$ | $S^2\setminus\{2\text{ pts}\} \cong S^1\times\mathbb{R}$ | $F_1 = \mathbb{Z}$ | $\mathbb{Z}$ ✓ |
| $(1,0)$ | Torus $T^2$ | $\langle a,b\mid [a,b]=1\rangle \cong \mathbb{Z}^2$ | $\mathbb{Z}^2$ ✓ |
| $(1,1)$ | Once-punctured torus | $F_{2}$ | $F_2$ ✓ |

---

## Conclusion

$$\pi_1(S_{g,m}) \;\cong\; \begin{cases} \bigl\langle a_1,b_1,\dots,a_g,b_g \;\big|\; [a_1,b_1]\cdots[a_g,b_g] = 1 \bigr\rangle, & m = 0, \\[6pt] F_{\,2g+m-1}, & m \geq 1, \end{cases}$$

where $F_r$ denotes the free group of rank $r$ (with $F_0$ the trivial group). Equivalently, for **all** $m \geq 0$ the group admits the unified presentation

$$\pi_1(S_{g,m}) = \bigl\langle a_1,b_1,\dots,a_g,b_g,\,c_1,\dots,c_m \;\big|\; [a_1,b_1]\cdots[a_g,b_g]\,c_1\cdots c_m = 1 \bigr\rangle,$$

which reduces to the closed surface group when $m=0$ and to the free group $F_{2g+m-1}$ when $m \geq 1$ (by eliminating one generator via the single relation).
